title: Anchored tone scale with asymmetric radius system for dense controls and charts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Aim: Deliver a token set that preserves contrast and perceived depth at high visual density while enabling smaller radii on action controls and tighter spacing for table rows and chart overlays.

Scope: color token anchors (neutral and semantic ramps), typographic micro-scale for dense contexts (label, caption, micro), proportional spacing rhythm (1px base grid with fractional scales), an asymmetric radius system (corner deltas for primary vs secondary controls), and a shadow/elevation translation strategy that compresses depth for dense surfaces.

Outcomes:
- Single source tokens for Anchors (neutrals 0-9) with computed deltas for density contexts
- Micro typographic scale added to token catalog: micro-caption, micro-label, micro-mono
- Asymmetric radius tokens: radius-primary, radius-secondary, radius-chip with top/bottom deltas
- Compressed elevation tokens for dense surfaces: elevation-1-compact .. elevation-5-compact

Design trade-offs considered: preserving accessible contrast vs maintaining compactness; decided to keep AA contrast for text but allow reduced contrast for decorative accents; asymmetric radii optimize tap targets by keeping interactive top-left corners larger while allowing smaller outer radii for stacked lists.

This ticket focuses on the token definitions, token usage guidance, migration plan, and Figma token library updates. Engineering implementation (runtime bundling, CSS variables, theme compiler) is tracked in dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: Tokens checked into token-registry JSON and published to the token CDN
Design tokens documented in the Tokens Guide with usage examples for buttons, tables, chips, and chart legends
Figma file updated with token styles and three example component instances (dense table row, compact toolbar, stacked chips)
Cross-browser visual regression run showing < 2px layout shifts across tokens at three breakpoints
A11y check: body and caption text pass WCAG AA contrast in dense mode; guidance doc recorded exceptions
Engineering sign-off: ENG-45220 implements CSS variables and theme fallback; visual diff approved
comments: 2025-02-18 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed on the need for asymmetric radii to reduce perceived bulk on stacked controls. Chose 1px base grid to keep hairline separators crisp in dense tables.
2025-02-21 - Liam Chen: Added initial token draft to Figma. Shared early comp for compact table with product and got direction to preserve label contrast at small sizes.
2025-02-26 - Maya Ortiz (PM): Request to include chart legend micro-typography and to ensure embeddable chart components don't inherit large global radii.
2025-03-01 - Liam Chen: Updated token JSON and opened PR to token-registry: https://github.com/redwood-inference/token-registry/pull/224 (needs ENG review).
2025-03-02 - Design review: approved token names and deltas; noted need for migration guide and an automated codemod for legacy CSS classes.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Publish tokens to registry under 'compact' flavor. Phase 2: Ship CSS variable aliases for old token names + deprecation timeline (4 weeks). Phase 3: Run automated codemod to swap usages in classic components; manual audit for third-party embeds. Rollout: default behind feature flag 'ui.compactTokens' for 2 weeks before global enablement.
qa_checklist: 1) Validate token JSON schema and lint. 2) Verify Figma styles reflect tokens and are using shared components. 3) Run visual diffs for primary components (buttons, table, chart legend) across desktop/tablet/mobile. 4) Accessibility contrast audit for micro typography in dense mode. 5) Verify theme fallback for Private deployments where token CDN is blocked.
